what_happened: The job rewrote owner decision cards so each has a question and outcomes that depend on the proposal. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict with one blocker and two major findings. No acceptance criteria or checks are listed as unmet or failed. The blocker: `plain_words` loops forever on any title containing "implementation", which would hang the whole site build. Major finding 1: the verb-first test uses a word list that includes words often used as nouns, so many problem titles turn into garbled questions. Major finding 2: jargon is replaced word by word, which produces nonsense titles, and a test fixes one of them as the expected output.
cause: The decision-card work is built from text-rewriting rules (verb lists, jargon swaps) that are judged only by a few fixtures the producer chose. Nothing in the reading, plan or checks runs the renderer over every real open proposal title. Nothing requires a termination or garble check on arbitrary input. The expected-output test is written from the rule's own output, so it confirms the rule and not that the text reads well. The last two rejections in this renderer area (20261103-074940-hcey, 20261103-235051-6bj9) had the same root: the card text was never checked against real proposals. The lesson stayed in individual rejections and did not become a check.
prevention: Add a standing test in xtask that renders a card for every real proposal title in the repo (the decisions and proposals files, not fixtures) under a time limit. It must finish, and each output must pass mechanical checks: no repeated or leftover jargon tokens, a question that ends with a question mark, and no title that is empty or unchanged by a failed rule. The test must run in the normal workspace gate, so a hang or garbled output fails before the verifier. Any rewrite rule must be a single pass with a bounded loop.
proposed_request:
Fix the decision-card question builder in xtask/src/decisions.rs. Outcome: the site build never hangs, and every real open proposal gets a card question that reads as plain English.

Acceptance:
- `plain_words` terminates on every input. A test runs it on titles containing "implementation", repeated jargon words and empty strings, and each call finishes.
- The jargon rewrite works on whole phrases, not single words. No title comes out as nonsense, and the test that expects a garbled title is replaced with one that expects a readable title.
- The verb-first check no longer treats words that are usually nouns as verbs. A test covers titles that begin with such nouns, and each becomes a sensible question.
- A test renders a card for every real proposal title in the repo, not fixtures. It checks that each question is non-empty, ends in "?", contains no leftover jargon token, and differs between proposals with different titles. The test lists any title that fails.
- `cargo test --workspace`, clippy and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Evidence cites commands that ran.

Do not change card layout or anything outside xtask/src/decisions.rs and its tests.
